subject: ArrTags release candidate 0.1.0, re-audited after the SEC-1 fix (release code at commit c980b1f 'Fix SEC-1: authenticate webhook before request body binding'; repository HEAD ccb17f4, whose only later commits touch docs/implementation/final-review/; installed artifact artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip, 568,244 bytes, SHA-256 f6b6a515c76b93926e940cebd48918f864935893b2ae7d03f59b17e38e0f9ffd, 7 entries)

findings.area: webhook HTTP boundary / input handling (authenticate-before-body and payload bound)
findings.description: FIXED and independently verified. The pre-fix defect was that the anonymous webhook actions caused MVC model binding to materialize the composite value provider, which read/parsed form and multipart request bodies before the action's shared-secret check, so unauthenticated form/multipart requests returned a framework 400 and the body could be read up to Kestrel's 30,000,000-byte cap instead of the configured OperationalLimits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes (default 262,144 B). Commit c980b1f adds WebhookAuthenticationFilter, an IAsyncAuthorizationFilter applied with [TypeFilter(typeof(WebhookAuthenticationFilter))] on ArrTagsWebhookController. MVC runs authorization filters before model binding, so the filter now authenticates the X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header through the same bounded (1024-char) constant-time WebhookAuthentication/SecretLease path and fails closed with the uniform 401 before any body read for every content type, then rejects a declared non-JSON content type with a bounded 400 before the read. Independently reproduced on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host with the artifact installed: every unauthenticated request returned 401 for JSON (small and 300,000 B), x-www-form-urlencoded (small and 300,000 B), multipart/form-data (300,000 B and 36,700,000 B), text/plain, application/octet-stream, and absent content type, and for missing, wrong, and 2000-char candidates; the 36,700,000-byte unauthenticated multipart request returned 401 in 0.4276 ms (X-Response-Time-ms), which is only possible if the body was never read. Authenticated behavior is bounded by the configured limit: 300,000-byte JSON (declared, chunked, and absent content type) returned 413, and 300,000-byte form/multipart returned the pre-read bounded 400. JSON behavior is otherwise unchanged (valid 202, malformed 400, oversized 413, unauth 401, charset/+json accepted). No secret or body was reflected in any response. The action retains its own authentication and byte bound as defence in depth.

findings.description: Unchanged and still present (the SEC-1 fix touched only the webhook boundary). When IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found, CreateStateRepository roots the entire authoritative plugin state at Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") - a predictable, shared location where another local user could pre-create or observe a same-named directory. It is not triggered on the pinned host (the plugin is found and DataFolderPath is ProgramDataPath/ArrTags; live check: /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags does not exist) and is not remotely reachable. Not a release blocker.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:178-180 (string.IsNullOrEmpty(plugin?.DataFolderPath) ? Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") : plugin!.DataFolderPath)
live: ls /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags -> No such file or directory after the full webhook matrix
findings.recommended_action: Fail closed (do not register state-dependent services) or use a host-private directory when the plugin data folder cannot be resolved, instead of a shared temp path.

findings.description: Unchanged. The versioned state envelope's SHA-256 (PayloadSha256) covers only PayloadJson; envelope metadata (SchemaVersion, Kind, RecordId, Authority, Terminal, UpdatedUtc) is not covered. Retention trusts the unauthenticated Terminal and UpdatedUtc fields. This is not an escalation: local write access to the state root is already the administrative boundary and such a writer could delete files directly, so the guarantee is corruption detection rather than tamper authentication. No code in this area changed in the fix.
evidence: src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:83-113 (hash compared only against parsed.PayloadJson)
src/ArrTags/State/StateRetention.cs:154-165 (retention reads envelope.Terminal/UpdatedUtc)
findings.recommended_action: None required for the release; optionally cover the envelope metadata in the integrity hash or document StateEnvelopeCodec as a corruption detector rather than a tamper MAC.

findings.description: Re-adjudicated after the fix. The fix removed the pre-auth framework form-limit detail that the attempt-1 audit observed ('Form key length limit 2048 exceeded', 'Request body too large. The max request body size is 30000000 bytes') because non-JSON bodies are now rejected before any parse. The remaining behavior is the already-documented limitation D1: every webhook failure returns an ASP.NET Core [ApiController] application/problem+json ProblemDetails body with only type, title, status, and traceId (401 Unauthorized, 400 Bad Request, 413 Content Too Large), while ADR-012 still says authentication failures return 'no body'. Independently observed: all unauthenticated failures are a uniform 165-byte body and all authenticated bounded rejections a uniform 164/171-byte body; no secret, header, candidate, body, route, plugin, or item-existence detail is reflected. This is the same class as D1, extended to the authenticated non-JSON 400.
evidence: live results: u01/u03/u06 401 bodies = {"type":".../rfc9110#section-15.5.2","title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"traceId":...} (uniform, 165 bytes); a04/a06 400 and a05 413 bodies likewise generic
docs/limitations.md D1 (lines 302-314) documents the 401 body versus ADR-012 wording gap
docs/decisions.md ADR-012 still states every authentication failure returns the same bounded 401 'with no body'
findings.recommended_action: None required; optionally normalise error responses to a minimal body and correct the ADR-012 'no body' wording (already tracked as D1).

findings.description: Unchanged. The Sonarr/Radarr API keys and the inbound webhook shared secret are persisted only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML and returned by Jellyfin's authenticated, elevation-gated plugin-configuration API to administrators (accepted ADR-005 single-source-of-truth design). Independent re-check: no configured key or secret appears in the host log, the state root, or the release artifact; the only host file containing them is data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml. The plugin still has zero ILogger/Console/log call sites, so no plugin log path can leak a secret.

findings.description: Unchanged. Accepted limitation D2: ArtworkSubjectGate.Gates is a process-lifetime static ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> with no eviction, keyed by (Jellyfin item id, image surface), which is not attacker-controllable and is bounded in practice by the host's distinct library items. Webhook intake/coalescing, the work queue, reconciliation batches, provider response reads, artifact reads/writes, decoded dimensions, JSON depth, and episode entries all remain explicitly bounded.

findings.area: webhook HTTP boundary / behavior change introduced by the fix
findings.description: Tracked behavior change from the SEC-1 fix, as required. After authentication, a declared non-JSON content type is now rejected with a bounded 400 before any read (pre-fix, form/multipart were framework-parsed and text/plain/octet-stream bodies were read and parsed by the action). Concretely, a syntactically valid JSON payload sent with a non-JSON content type such as text/plain now returns 400 instead of 202. A missing content type is still tolerated and treated as JSON (202/400/413 as appropriate), and application/json, text/json, and +json structured suffixes are accepted. Sonarr and Radarr send application/json, so no real delivery is affected. The choice of 400 rather than 415 is deliberate (matches the existing ADR-012 payload-rejection status) and is recorded in the worker known_limitations.
evidence: live: authenticated text/plain small -> 400 (a09); authenticated application/octet-stream small -> 400 (a10); authenticated absent content type small valid JSON -> 202 (f01); authenticated Application/JSON -> 202 (e05); application/vnd.api+json -> 202 (e06)
src/ArrTags/Webhooks/WebhookAuthenticationFilter.cs:66-98 (non-JSON rejection and IsJsonContentType acceptance set)
docs/implementation/release-0.1.0-sec1/worker-report.json known_limitations
findings.recommended_action: None required; documented. If a future provider sends a non-JSON content type, revisit whether 415 is preferable.

findings.description: Observation, not a defect. The anonymous webhook route applies no ArrTags-level per-client throttling to authentication attempts (the ADR-012 'rate limiting' is bounded intake/coalescing of accepted deliveries, not auth throttling). The exposure is mitigated by the high-entropy administrator-configured shared secret, the 1024-character candidate bound, the constant-time compare, and the uniform fail-closed 401 that reveals nothing; the only shared-state cost per attempt is two short ConfigurationSnapshotService lock acquisitions (Current and TryAcquire) with no unbounded allocation. This property is unchanged by the fix (the filter adds one more bounded compare/lock pair per request) and was accepted in the attempt-1 audit. No action required for V1.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Webhooks/WebhookAuthentication.cs:61-92 (bounded candidate, constant-time compare, uniform outcome)
src/ArrTags/Configuration/ConfigurationSnapshotService.cs:54-63,94-110 (short lock-guarded snapshot read and lease acquisition)
docs/decisions.md ADR-012 'Rate limiting and coalescing' (bounded intake/coalescing, not per-client auth throttling)
findings.recommended_action: None required; optional post-V1 per-source throttling or reverse-proxy rate limiting.

summary: Independent adversarial re-audit of ArrTags 0.1.0 after the SEC-1 fix (release code c980b1f, HEAD ccb17f4; artifact 568,244 bytes / SHA-256 f6b6a515...) found no open BLOCKER or HIGH and no open MEDIUM. SEC-1 is genuinely fixed and was reproduced on the actual pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl runtime path: the new pre-model-binding WebhookAuthenticationFilter authenticates before any body read, so every unauthenticated request - JSON, form-urlencoded, multipart, text/plain, octet-stream, or absent content type - now returns the uniform 401 (the 36.7 MB unauthenticated multipart case answered in 0.43 ms with no read), and the configured WebhookMaxPayloadBytes (256 KiB) is the effective bound for authenticated payloads (300,000-byte JSON -> 413 for declared, chunked, and absent content types). JSON behavior is unchanged (401/400/413/202), the filter uses the existing bounded 1024-char constant-time authentication and fails closed, and no plugin work or state occurs before authentication (no state root created; in-process tests assert zero body reads and zero intake). No secret or body is reflected. The fix introduced no new weakness; the only behavior change (authenticated declared non-JSON is now a bounded pre-read 400, so valid JSON with a non-JSON content type is rejected) is documented and tracked (SEC-7). The previously verified protections still hold: secrets are contained (zero logging call sites; only Jellyfin's config XML holds the values; artifact clean), state integrity is unchanged and byte-identical to the attempt-1 audit, input bounds are unchanged, and the provider integration remains GET-only. SEC-2 remains open LOW (shared-temp state-root fallback, unreachable in practice); SEC-3, SEC-4, SEC-5, and SEC-6 remain INFORMATIONAL (noted), with SEC-4 narrowed because the pre-auth framework form-limit detail is gone while the documented D1 problem+json body remains. reviewer_status APPROVED: no open BLOCKER, HIGH, or MEDIUM.
